subject: Billing: heartbeat offsets, call-priority, and rounding examples

Subject: Billing mechanics question: minimums, heartbeat, and short-response rounding

Hi Jasmine / Vanessa,

Quick follow-up from our call earlier — thanks for the overview. Before we sign the amendment we need clarity on two practical billing questions so our procurement team can map expected costs:

1) Short-response minimums: we have a lot of very short calls (e.g., status checks that return 8–12 tokens). How are those billed? Do those get rounded to a minimum quantum per call?

2) Heartbeat/prefill pings: our front-end sends keepalive calls every ~20s during an active chat session to keep KV warm. Are those pings billed the same way as normal generation calls? If they are small, do they repeatedly trigger the minimum?

Can you provide a simple invoice-style example: 24 short calls (9 tokens generated each) plus 3 long calls (2,000 tokens generated each) in the same day — how do the line items look after rounding/minimums and any aggregation?

Attaching our internal forecast and the current contract draft (sent to procurement). Appreciate a quick worked example we can share with Finance.

Thanks,
Sam
Director of Integrations
Acme Health

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Billing mechanics question: minimums, heartbeat, and short-response rounding

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Below is a concise, concrete explanation of how our billing interacts with short responses, heartbeats, and session aggregation (with worked numbers). Sharing so Finance can map it into your model.

Summary of Redwood billing primitives (TL;DR):
- Quantum: we bill generation in quanta of 64 tokens for this SKU. Every generation call is rounded up to the nearest 64-token quantum unless it is aggregated with other calls within the same aggregation window.
- Minimum per-call: a single discrete generation call that isn't aggregated will incur a 1-quantum minimum (64 tokens).
- Aggregation window: we support a 2-minute session aggregation window for conversation traffic (configurable on Dedicated). Calls that are part of the same session and arrive within the window are eligible to be summed and billed as a single quantum-rounded unit rather than each hitting the 1-quantum minimum individually.
- Heartbeats/prefill pings: treated as generation calls for billing purposes. If your keepalive returns a non-empty generation (e.g., a small prefill), it's counted and subject to the same quantum/minimum rules — unless the ping is configured as a non-billable KV-prefill (we can enable for pilots).
- KV/Prefix reuse: when the runtime can re-use KV cache (identical prefix tokens), those tokens are not recharged as new context generation; only newly generated tokens are billed. This reduces effective cost for repeated short replies.

Worked invoice-style example (your numbers):
Scenario: On 2026-08-12 you make 24 short calls that each generate 9 tokens AND 3 long calls that each generate 2,000 tokens. Assume all 24 short calls are within the same session and fall inside the 2-minute aggregation window in groups of 6 (i.e., 4 aggregated buckets).

Per-call math (policy above):
- Short calls: 24 calls x 9 tokens = 216 generated tokens total. If aggregated into 4 buckets, each bucket = 6 calls x 9 = 54 tokens. Each aggregated bucket rounds up to 1 quantum (64 tokens). So four buckets => billed tokens = 4 x 64 = 256 tokens.
- If short calls were NOT aggregated (worst case), each call would round up to 64 tokens => 24 x 64 = 1536 billed tokens. This is the difference aggregation removes.
- Long calls: 3 x 2000 = 6,000 tokens generated. Each long call is rounded up to nearest 64: 2000 / 64 = 31.25 -> round up to 32 quanta => 32 x 64 = 2048 billed tokens each. So 3 x 2048 = 6144 billed tokens.

Total billed tokens (aggregated case): 256 (shorts) + 6144 (longs) = 6400 billed tokens.
Total billed tokens (no aggregation): 1536 + 6144 = 7680 billed tokens.

Notes:
- The aggregation window is the lever that yields most savings for heavy short-call patterns.
- Heartbeats: if the 24 short calls are heartbeats that return 9 tokens and are spaced >2 minutes apart, they will be billed individually (worst case above). If they are within the window (or we enable non-billable KV prefill for your pilot), they will be aggregated.
- Pilot options: for pilots we can enable 'non-billable KV prefill' which converts keepalive prefills into non-billed cache-warm actions (still subject to rate limits but excluded from token billing).

I'll attach a simple spreadsheet with the line-by-line numbers. If you'd like, Vanessa can propose a pilot credit to offset the worst-case rounding for your first 30 days so Finance can model expected vs. invoiced.

Cheers,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-billing-examples.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Vanessa / Ben — forwarding Sam's ask and my worked math. Procurement wants a sample invoice and an option to mitigate worst-case rounding during the pilot. My proposed public-facing offer:

- Enable session aggregation (2-minute window) for Acme by default.
- For the first 30 days post-activation, provide a 50% credit on billed tokens that are due to per-call minimum rounding (i.e., the delta between raw generated tokens and rounded billed tokens for calls flagged as "short-response rounding impact").
- Enable KV-prefill non-billable for keepalives (pilot feature toggle) to reduce heartbeat costs.

If Ben can confirm the cost impact for us (estimate of credit liability from typical pilot volumes) I can send a one-page amendment (DocuSign) and the sample invoice line. I attached the spreadsheet with the example Jasmine prepared.

—Jasmine

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Billing mechanics question: minimums, heartbeat, and short-response rounding — Acme pilot offer and sample invoice

Hi Sam — thanks for the patience. Quick answers and the sample invoice line below. We're happy to run the pilot with the mitigations Jasmine proposed.

1) What if the 24 short calls are NOT aggregated?
- Non-aggregated billed tokens = 1536 (shorts) + 6144 (longs) = 7680 billed tokens.
- Aggregated billed tokens (best case) = 6400 billed tokens.
- Delta = 7680 - 6400 = 1280 billed tokens. At $0.0008 / billed token (as in draft amendment) that's $1.024 difference for that day's activity.

2) Non-billable KV prefill pilot:
- This is an account-level toggle we can enable for you for the pilot. It's implemented in the control plane (no code-change on your side). It removes small keepalive-prefill generations from billing while still warming KV. It does not change latency/SLAs in normal operation; we run a lightweight check to ensure it does not adversely affect cache hit behavior.

Sample invoice line (aggregated case) using $0.0008 / billed token: 
- Line: Redwood Inference — Token generation (aggregated 2026-08-12) — 6,400 billed tokens x $0.0008 = $5.12

Pilot offer (for procurement):
- Enable session aggregation + KV-prefill non-billable for 30 days.
- 50% credit on rounding delta for first 30 days. We'll capture the delta automatically and apply the credit on the following invoice.
- Amendment (one-page) linked here: https://www.docusign.com/ACME/amendment-002 (DocuSign).

If that matches your expectations, I'll send the amendment and a short note to Procurement to approve.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
